correctness.rationale: Finite \(d\)-multiorders have free one-point insertion slots in each coordinate. The pointwise-base signed-coordinate quotient is the product of symmetric groups over ranking classes modulo reversal (with the \(m=1\) exception). Its action on normalized slot vectors yields multiset coefficients; strictly decreasing ratios of binomial(m+r,r) prove sharp min/max and all equality cases, and \(m!/2\) distinct ranking classes yield the factorial threshold. The accompanying independent group-action enumerator passed 987 finite cases; its finiteness is not used to justify unrestricted claims.

Source inspection and published-finding corpus statement/implication comparison found no direct or stronger coverage; elementary implicit derivability remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Some elementary permutation-group actions may contain the multiset expression implicitly without indexed keywords.

value.rationale: Pointwise parameters in reducts must break hidden symmetries in a quantifiable way. This theorem classifies every possible one-type count from full ranking occupancy, supplies sharp minima/maxima and equality configurations for arbitrary dimension, and computes exactly how many named parameters are necessary to eliminate all signed coordinate symmetries. These are natural structural invariants and sharp thresholds, not a numerical slice chosen ad hoc.
